note: Reproduced exactly as sent, including the wording. The questions and figures in it are the same ones published on this page.

body.x: Dear George / KTFC Board,

I hope you are well. I am writing on behalf of the newly-forming Kettering Town FC Supporters' Association, a working group of supporters looking to help wade through the noise of social media to capture fan sentiment through hard and consistent data.

Our website, fans.ktfcsa.com, should give you a good overview of what we are looking to achieve and some of the features and functionalities built for fans, by fans. Our work is very carefully focused around trying to amplify fan voices while being very mindful of the good work done by the Trust.

Between Monday 17 and midday on Friday 21 August we asked Kettering Town supporters what they make of the way the club is being run. 199 people answered in five days. Anyone could take part, with or without an account, one response per device. Nobody was paid, prompted or selected. The full results, every figure and the method behind them, are published at fans.ktfcsa.com and will stay there.
We are writing because we told supporters we would put what they said directly to the club, in writing, and publish whatever comes back.
1. What supporters said
Confidence in how the club is being run stands at 2.4 out of ten. When the same question was put to this fanbase in May, it was 8.1.

x: Lowest score of 1 out of 10: 96 people
Scored 3 or less: 153 of 199
Scored 8 or more: 10 of 199
Club heading in the wrong direction: 151 of 199
Club heading in the right direction: 9 of 199
Not sure: 39 of 199

body.x: The concerns are concentrated rather than scattered:

x: Volunteers leaving: 184 of 199
The club's finances: 172 of 199
Communication with supporters: 171 of 199
Transparency: 148 of 199
Sponsors and partners: 143 of 199
The ground and facilities: 119 of 199
Matchday: 63 of 199

body.x: Asked how well each body represents them, supporters answered:

x: Club ownership: 83% poor or very poor
The club board: 71% poor or very poor
Club partners and sponsors: 53% poor or very poor

body.x: We would ask you not to read these as the usual noise. The same fanbase gave a score of 8.1 only three months ago.
2. What this is not
Two findings cut against the general mood and we publish them as plainly as the rest.

The team is the single most praised thing about the club, named by 168 of 199 supporters. The criticism here is aimed at how the club is run. It is not aimed at the players, the manager, or the staff who turn up every week.
The Supporters' Trust, whose role several supporters raised, is rated good or very good by more people than rate it poorly.

We have also held back eight submissions in full. Some carried allegations we are not in a position to stand up, and some were not appropriate to pass on. They have not been sent to you and they have not been published. That is not us protecting anyone. It is us keeping this to what can reasonably be answered.
3. The questions
Supporters submitted 109 questions. We have grouped them into the ten below. The wording of each is ours; the number beside it is how many supporters asked that question in one form or another.
The ten questions are listed in full above, each with the number of supporters who asked it and how long it has gone unanswered.
Addendum
Six questions did not fall under any of the above. They are reproduced here in supporters' own words so that nothing asked is left out.

x: How sustainable are the squad we have?
When will the club go back to being the club I went to watch twice a week, and love being part of.
What is the most important asset of a football club? If your answer is its Supporters, do you acknowledge that many of those Supporters are here due to the excellent work of Phil Wade?
What is the reason that George and his family are here?
Don't let us lose this once in a generation opportunity with Brad. Leave the club with your head held high after playoffs and FA Cup run.
When will the website be updated, do we not have anyone working on it?

body.x: 4. A reply
We would kindly ask for a reply by Friday 4 September 2026.

The results page publishes which of these questions have been answered and how long any unanswered question has been outstanding. That page updates itself. We would far rather it recorded answers than days.
5. What we would like to happen next

181 of the 199 supporters who answered said they would attend a first meeting of the Supporters' Association, 118 of them in person. That is the clearest single result in the whole exercise, and it is a constructive one. Supporters are not asking to run the club. They are asking to be told things.

For transparency, a copy of this open letter will be shared to the KTFC Supporters' Association website and social media pages shortly, alongside the full list of questions and the time and date sent.

We are aware that supporters have discussed forms of protest, and the report records what they said they would support, including 86 who backed a boycott. We report that because it is what the data shows. We are not calling for any of it, and we would much rather report that these questions were answered, and answered fully.
We would welcome a meeting or with the board, at a time of your choosing, and we would publish an account of it either way.

The Supporters' Association is independent of the club, takes no money from it, and speaks only for the supporters who answered. The group is in its infancy, but interest in the initiative has been encouraging, and we are now looking to arrange a first meeting in person.
We have no interest in a battle with Kettering Town Football Club. We have an interest in it being run well and a hope that the work being done can be leveraged to ultimately enhance fan experience.

x: Yours sincerely,
Danny Jordan
On behalf of the newly-formed Kettering Town FC Supporters' Association working group
